problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}20 \\ -20 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.
worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{20\cdot 4+(-20)\cdot 5+0\cdot 0}{{4}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{1}=-\frac{20}{41}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{20\cdot 5+(-20)\cdot (-4)+0\cdot 0}{{5}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{180}{41}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =-\frac{20}{41}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+\frac{180}{41}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{20}{41}(-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+9[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}20 \\ -20 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** The projection is the vector $x$ itself. This means that $x$ can be written as a linear combination of ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$ In other words, $x$ lies in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$
